messages:
maria: FYI I'm seeing intermittent 15-25% token latency spikes on FlashAttention when seq lengths hop between 512 and 1024 in the same batch. repro script attached below. Can someone run a focused microbench with the fused-op path disabled/enabled and KV-prefetch toggled? PR reference: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/432

ryan: on it. which HW and driver stack?

maria: 4xA100 (80GB) on prod-like kernel, CUDA 12.1 + cuDNN 9.1. I reproduced locally on 2xA100 as well.

ryan: got it. I'll run on pool-prod-8 (same driver). quick command I'll use:
```bash
./bench --model gpt2-xl --seqs "512,1024" --batches 100 --batch-sizes "4,8" --flash=true --fused_kernels=true --kv_prefetch=true
```

cheng: I can also try toggling the attention tile size to see if misalignment causes extra kernel launches. ping me the exact commit.

maria: top of main + the perf flag change in that PR (link above).

perf-bot: Benchmark job queued (id=98765) by ryan on pool-prod-8. ETA ~12m. Logs streaming: https://perf.redwood.ai/jobs/98765

samir: quick note — when we ran a similar variability before it turned out to be a fallback to generic softmax kernel for certain seq mod 128 cases. worth checking kernel selection logs (env var RL_DEBUG_KERNEL=1).

ryan: good call, enabling that now. also will run with fused_kernels=false to compare.

maria: also try batch composition where all sequences are padded to same length (pad-to-max) vs mixed lengths. that helped in the past.

cheng: I'll instrument runtime to dump kernel names + launch times (small patch) and post a diff here in ~30m.

perf-bot: Benchmark job started (id=98765).

ryan: initial pass looks like ~18% p50 token latency spike when fused_kernels=true & mixed lengths. with fused_kernels=false it's down to baseline. attaching a snippet from the bench:
```
[info] kernel=flash_attn_fused -- launch 12.3ms
[info] kernel=generic_softmax -- launch 28.7ms
[info] seq_length=1024 batch_idx=7
```

maria: hmm that suggests fused path sometimes triggers a fallback to generic softmax for certain tiles. Cheng's patch might confirm.

cheng: confirmed — kernel selection logic chooses a different tiling for mixed-lengths which ends up calling a slower generic kernel in some micro-batches. patch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/438 (adds a conservative tile alignment check and logs).

samir: can we add an automated microbench that runs mixed-length warmups and checks for kernel fallbacks as a regression guard?

maria: yes please. If we catch it in CI we'll avoid surprises on Dedicated. Ryan/cheng can you create a small test in perf-suite (bench/regressions/mixed_kernel_fallback_test.cc) that flags >5% regression?

ryan: will do. I'll also add a quick canary rollout config to route 5% traffic to fused_kernels=true on dedicated so we can observe in prod traces without full exposure.

maria: sweet. timeline: get kernel logs + patch in today, add perf test tomorrow, roll canary early next week. thanks all :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Benchmark job finished (id=98765). summary: fused_kernels=true mixed-lengths: +18% p50 tokens. fused_kernels=false: baseline. Full report: https://perf.redwood.ai/reports/98765

ryan: created draft perf test and opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/perf-suite/pull/77 — includes synthetic mixed-length workload and asserts no kernel fallback.

cheng: merged kernel-selection logging patch to main and uploaded a flame graph for the failing micro-batch to the ticket.

maria: excellent. after perf test merges let's coordinate a short docs blurb for engineers about recommended padding policy and an alert rule for kernel fallback rate >1% on Dedicated.

samir: I'll file an observability task in Jira and tag infra/alerting.

maria: thanks team. ping me if any of the runs show different hardware behavior (e.g., H100).
